missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Root Storm. The root network has been so compromised by rot, curses, and corrupted geas that it has begun to fight itself. The roots are growing against each other — each one trying to fulfill a different corrupted binding.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Storm-driven roots attacking anything that moves. Each root is fulfilling a corrupted geas — binding, crushing, or dissolving. They do not distinguish friend from foe. They only fulfill.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The storm-driven roots attack without discrimination. Do not fight the roots — fight the singers. The roots are victims of the corrupted geas, not enemies.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The storm is calmed — but the root network is devastated. Half the roots are dead. The surviving roots carry the scars. The forest will regrow — but slowly, and with memory.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The storm-driven roots overwhelmed you. You fought the roots instead of the singers. Return when the weapon is the song, not the root.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Root Storm tests whether the deity can calm a living system that is destroying itself. The roots are not enemies — they are victims of corrupted geas. The Hollow's strategy: turn the support system against itself, so the road destroys its own foundation.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The root-storm is intensifying. Roots are tearing through the Sídhe Mound, destroying each other. The violence is the Hollow's design — each root that dies feeds the void. The root network is consuming itself.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The roots are combining attacks. Multiple corrupted geas create compound root-attacks — bindings that crush while dissolving. The duality is the weapon.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The compound root-attacks bind and dissolve simultaneously. You cannot escape both — but you can cut the geas that drives them. Cut the song, not the root.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The compound root-attacks are stopped — but the corrupted geas lingers in the surviving roots. Each root could reignite at any time. The deeper chambers will test whether the calm holds.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The compound root-attacks bound and dissolved simultaneously. You could not escape both. Return when cutting the geas is faster than cutting the root.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The compound root-attacks — binding and dissolving simultaneously — are the Tuatha Gate's most painful weapon: the support system attacking from two directions at once. The deity cannot fight the roots without wounding the forest. The only solution is to cut the geas, not the root.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The storm has reached the trial road. Roots burst through the ground without warning, binding and crushing. The deity must walk a road that is being destroyed by the very system meant to support it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow root-singers. They sing corrupted geas to the roots, driving the storm. Each song is a binding that makes roots fight. The singers are the storm's engine.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The root-singers drive the storm with corrupted geas. Silence the singers — but carefully. Killing a singer releases its geas into the nearest root, making it stronger.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The root-singers are silenced — but their songs echo in the root network. The echoes could reawaken the storm. The deeper chambers will be louder with corrupted geas.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The root-singers' songs drove the storm faster than you could silence them. Each dead singer made the nearest root stronger. Return when silencing is not killing.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The root-singers are the storm's engine. Each song is a corrupted geas that drives roots to violence. Silencing a singer is necessary — but killing a singer releases its geas into the nearest root. The deity must silence without killing — the Tuatha art of stopping the song without ending the singer.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The storm's eye. The original root — the first geas — is the only root not fighting. It stands at the center of the storm, untouched. But it is shrinking. Every root that dies takes a piece of the original with it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The storm's eye guardian — a Hollow standing beside the original root, singing the one song that would calm the storm. But the song is inverted: it would calm the roots by killing them all at once.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The guardian sings the inverted calming song. Do not let it finish — the song would calm the roots by killing them. Sing the original: the song that calms by healing, not by ending.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The storm's eye is reclaimed. The original root is alive — diminished, but alive. The calming song is restored. But the root network is half-dead, and the dead roots feed the void.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The guardian's inverted calming song was almost complete. You could not sing the original in time. Return when healing is faster than ending.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The storm's eye — the original root untouched by the storm — reveals the Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: the foundation does not fight. It stands. Every root that fights has been corrupted. The original root simply exists. The calm is not the absence of violence — it is the presence of the original.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns. The final trial. The Hollow has grown a crown from the corrupted roots — a geas-crown that binds whoever wears it to the void. The crown sits on the original root, poisoning it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns. Each thorn is a corrupted geas that embeds deeper with movement. The more you struggle, the tighter it binds. The crown wants you to move.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown tightens with movement. Do not struggle. Approach without moving — through will, not through the body. The crown wants you to fight. Refuse to fight.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The crown is transformed. The thorns that bound now graft. The geas that cursed now heals. The original root is saved — and the crown is part of it now. The Silver-Root Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown tightened with every movement. You struggled. Return when stillness is more powerful than struggle.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is the Tuatha Gate's ultimate test: can the deity save a living system by transforming the weapon that destroys it? The crown cannot be removed without killing the root. It cannot stay without killing the root. The third option is transformation — wearing the crown and turning the binding into a healing.

missionIntro.text: The geas-crown is tightening. Each thorn is a corrupted geas that embeds deeper with every movement. The deity must approach the crown without moving — or the thorns tighten and the root dies.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The crown is spawning thorn-constructs from the original root's bark. Each one is a piece of the root that has been consumed. They attack because the root's own geas is inverted.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The thorn-constructs are pieces of the root. Do not destroy them — they are the root. Dispel the inversion, not the bark. The root's geas is corrupted, but the bark is still the root's.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The thorn-constructs are restored to the root. The bark that fought now supports. The inversion is reversed — not by force, but by transformation. The root chose the original song.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The thorn-constructs were pieces of the root. You destroyed them. Return when the root's bark is not the enemy, even when it fights you.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The geas-crown's thorns embed deeper with movement. The Hollow's strategy: provoke struggle. The more the deity fights, the tighter the binding. The defense is stillness — approaching through will, not through the body. The crown wants you to fight. The root needs you to be still.

missionIntro.text: The crown has consumed the original root's first geas. The binding that sustained the forest — 'I bind the void to the forest' — is now 'I bind the forest to the void.' The crown speaks the inversion as law.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow crown-singers. They sing the inverted geas — 'I bind the forest to the void' — in the original root's voice. The root hears its own voice serving the Hollow.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown-singers sing in the root's voice. Do not silence them — sing the original louder. The root must hear both songs and choose. The choice is the root's — not yours.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The crown-singers' inversion is silenced — not by violence, but by the louder original. The root heard both songs and chose to heal. The choice was the root's. The deity's role was to sing.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown-singers' inversion was louder than your original. You tried to silence them. Return when the original song is louder because it is true.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The crown-singers sing the inverted geas in the root's own voice. The root hears its own voice serving the Hollow. The defense is not silence — it is a louder original. The root must hear both songs and choose. The choice is the root's. The deity's role is to sing.

missionIntro.text: The final confrontation. The crown cannot be removed without killing the root — and the root cannot survive with the crown. The deity must find a third option: wear the crown and transform it, or let the root die and regrow from the corpse.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The crown itself — a living geas that has consumed the root's foundation. It cannot be removed without killing the root. It cannot stay without killing the root. The third option is the only way.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown cannot be removed or left. Find the third option. Wear the crown and transform it from within — turn the binding into a healing. The thorns that bind can also graft. The geas that curses can also cure.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is transformed into a Healing Crown. The third option was found: the binding that kills also heals, if worn with intention. The geas is not broken — it is redirected. The Silver-Root Gate stands.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown could not be removed or left. You saw no third option. Return when wearing the crown and transforming it from within is visible — when the binding that kills also heals.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: the binding that kills also heals, if worn with intention. The geas that curses can also cure. The thorns that bind can also graft. The third option is not a compromise — it is a transformation. The crown is not removed. It is worn. And the wearing changes both the crown and the wearer. The root is saved — and the crown is part of it now.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite root-rot wraiths carrying your Normal campaign geas-data. They know which bindings you cut and which you left — and they target the ones you spared.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The wraiths target the roots you spared in the Normal campaign. Do not protect the same roots — the Hollow expects it. Find new roots to heal.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: Chapter 1 holds — but the root network has recorded this healing too. The deeper chambers will test whether the new approach is real or simply a new pattern.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The wraiths targeted the roots you spared. You protected the same roots. Return when your healing is not pattern — it is creation.

missionIntro.text: The corrupted roots now carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence. Each cut you made to save the forest is now a vulnerability the Hollow can exploit.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The corrupted roots carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence against you. Each cut is proof you harmed the forest.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The wounds are evidence. Do not defend your cuts — demonstrate new healing. The root does not remember the intention. It remembers the wound.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The corrupted roots are calmed — but they recorded your new healing. The Hollow studies healing across campaigns.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The wounds were evidence against you. You defended your cuts. Return when new healing is more powerful than defending old wounds.

codex.text: The Gate's learning engine spans multiple campaigns. Each descent teaches the Hollow which roots the deity heals and how — and each lesson is a future weapon.

missionIntro.text: The Sídhe Mound expects your Normal campaign healing approach. Every technique you used to redirect, calm, or transform has been analyzed and countered.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The root-singers expect your Normal campaign calming approach. They have counter-songs for every technique that worked before.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The counter-songs are designed for your Normal campaign approach. Sing a new song — one the Hollow has not heard.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The counter-songs are silenced — but the root-singers heard your new song. The deeper chambers will have counter-songs for it too.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker

victory.text: The healing-singers fall silent. The new healing has no opposite — because it belongs to no one. The crown cannot invert what has no inverse. The healing is the act. The act is the healer's.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The healing-singers inverted your song. You tried to silence them. Return when a healing with no opposite is possible.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The healing-singers invert the deity's song. The inversion reveals the Hollow's deepest Tuatha strategy: every healing has an opposite, and the Hollow knows them all. The defense is a healing with no opposite — healing that belongs to no one, that has no owner, that exists only in the act.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Crow-Crowned Geas Breaker. Enter Crow-Crowned Heartwood on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Crow-Crowned Heartwood.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The final Elite confrontation. The crown's ultimate claim: your Normal campaign healing proves the crown can heal anything — including the Hollow. Disprove it — with healing that serves the root, not the crown.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The final crown — wearing your Normal campaign healing as its crown. The ultimate claim: healing belongs to the crown. Disprove it.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown claims your healing belongs to it. Disprove it — with healing that has no owner. Healing that belongs to the act, not the healer. The crown cannot consume what has no owner.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is destroyed for the last time. The ultimate claim is disproved: healing does not belong to the crown. Healing belongs to the act — and the act is the deity's. The crown was the instrument. The deity was the healer. The root was the healed. All three were needed. None owned the healing.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown claimed your healing. You argued. Return when healing that belongs to no one is more powerful than any claim.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Elite Final Verdict: healing belongs to the act, not the healer, not the instrument, not the crown. The crown was the instrument. The deity was the healer. The root was the healed. None owned the healing — because healing is not a possession. It is an action. And actions cannot be consumed, only repeated. The crown consumed the healing. The deity performed a new one. The crown could not consume what it had never seen — because the new healing had no owner, and what has no owner cannot be stolen.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Choir-Vault Threshold. Enter Choir-Vault Resonance Entry on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Choir-Vault Resonance Entry.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Choir-Vault Gate reopens. The celestial choir that once sustained divine order is silent. The Hollow consumed the singers' voices. Without the choir, the Gate's harmonics are destabilizing.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Silence-wraiths born from consumed choir voices. They do not attack — they silence. In their presence, the deity's harmony fades.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The silence-wraiths fade your harmony. Do not fight silence with sound — fight it with resonance. Resonance needs truth, not volume.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first choir-loft is restored. The silence is pushed back — but the choir is still voiceless. The road ahead requires more resonance than volume.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The silence-wraiths faded your harmony. You fought silence with sound. Return when resonance is more powerful than volume.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Choir-Vault Gate tests whether the deity can sustain divine order without the choir. The Hollow consumed the choir because it was shared. Individual harmony is harder to consume.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Choir-Vault Threshold. Enter Choir-Vault Resonance Entry on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Choir-Vault Resonance Entry.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The silence is spreading. Each empty choir-loft releases dissonance — the absence of harmony. In the Empyrean Gate, silence is not peace. Silence is dissolution.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The silence-wraiths are multiplying. The combined silence is heavy — like sound, but inverted. It presses against the deity's armor.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The combined silence presses against your armor. Do not push back — resonate. Silence is heavy because it is empty. Resonance is light because it is full.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The silence-wraiths are dispersed — but the silence lingers. The deeper chambers will be quieter still.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The combined silence crushed you. You pushed back instead of resonating. Return when fullness is lighter than emptiness is heavy.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The silence-wraiths are born from consumed voices. The silence is heavy because it is the weight of everything that should be there but is not. The defense is resonance — not volume, but truth.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The dissonance has reached the trial road. Each step requires the deity to generate their own harmony without the choir. The road dissolves where the harmony is weak.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow anti-singers. They produce anti-harmony — the exact inverse of the choir's original song. The anti-harmony cancels the deity's attempts to sing.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The anti-singers cancel your song. Do not sing louder — sing differently. A new harmony cannot be cancelled by an anti-song built for the original.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The anti-singers are silenced — but their anti-harmony echoes. The deeper chambers will have anti-songs for every harmony you have used.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The anti-singers cancelled your every song. You sang louder instead of differently. Return when a new harmony is more powerful than a louder one.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The anti-singers produce anti-harmony — the exact inverse of the choir's original song. The defense is a new harmony — one the anti-song was not built to cancel. Creation defeats inversion.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The choir's core. The first singer's voice is still intact — buried under layers of consumed silence. The Hollow wrapped the silence around it like a prison.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The first singer's prison guardian — a Hollow made of concentrated silence. It wraps tighter around the first voice with every sound the deity makes.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian tightens the prison with every sound. Do not sing to free the first voice — resonate with it. The first voice is still singing inside. Find its frequency.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first singer's prison is cracked. The voice inside is still singing — faint, but alive. That note is the foundation of the entire choir.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The guardian's prison tightened with your every sound. You sang to free the voice. Return when resonance can match a frequency without making it louder.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The first singer's note is the foundation of the entire choir. The Hollow wrapped it in silence because silence is the only prison that can hold a voice.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Memory-Burn Radiance. Enter Memory-Burn Corridor on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Memory-Burn Corridor.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Lightfall. The celestial light that sustains the Empyrean Gate is falling — not dimming, but literally falling in shards. Each shard of fallen light becomes a Hollow construct.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Fallen-light constructs. Each one is a shard of celestial light, Hollow-corrupted. They are made of the same light that sustains the Empyrean — fighting them weakens you.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The fallen-light constructs are made of your own light. Do not destroy them — reclaim them. The corruption is the enemy, not the light.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first lightfall is slowed. Some shards are reclaimed — but the sky is still darker. The road ahead requires self-generated light.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The constructs were made of your light. You destroyed them and weakened yourself. Return when reclamation is more powerful than destruction.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Lightfall tests whether the deity can sustain divine order when its source is being destroyed. The Hollow turns the source of power into the source of enemies.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield deity; roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Memory-Burn Radiance. Enter Memory-Burn Corridor on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Memory-Burn Corridor.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The lightfall is accelerating. Each fallen shard creates more constructs. The sky is darker. The constructs are more numerous. The deity fights in diminishing light against enemies made of the light itself.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The constructs are combining. Multiple shards merge into larger constructs. Each merged construct darkens the sky further.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The merged constructs darken the sky. Do not fight in the dark — generate your own light. Your light is not falling. It is you.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The merged constructs are separated — but the shards remain. The sky is dimmer. The deeper chambers will be darker still.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The merged constructs darkened the sky. You fought in the dark. Return when your radiance does not depend on the sky.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The fallen-light constructs are made of the deity's own power. The defense is reclamation — separating corruption from light and restoring the light to the sky.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The fallen light has reached the trial road. Each step is lit by shards — fragments of celestial light that now serve the Hollow. The road is bright, but the brightness is the enemy.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow light-eaters. They consume remaining celestial light by absorbing it. Each one makes the sky darker and themselves brighter. The brightness is the theft.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The light-eaters consume remaining light. Do not hoard the light — radiate it. Hoarded light can be eaten. Radiated light cannot. The light that is given is the light that remains.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The light-eaters are dispersed — but the consumed light is gone. The deity's own radiance must compensate.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The light-eaters consumed the light. You hoarded instead of radiating. Return when given light is more powerful than kept light.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The light-eaters consume by absorbing. The defense is radiance — giving light away. Hoarded light can be eaten. Radiated light cannot. The light that is given is the light that remains.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The lightfall source. The first lamp — the celestial light's origin. The Hollow has cracked it. Each crack releases more light as shards.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The cracked lamp guardian — a Hollow made of the first lamp's fragments. It guards the cracks because the cracks feed it.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian fights with the lamp's own light. Do not fight the light — fight the cracks. Seal the cracks from inside. The guardian starves when the light stops falling.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The cracked lamp is partially sealed — but the cracks are deep. The first lamp's light is restored — but dimmer. The light that fell cannot be fully reclaimed.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The guardian fought with the lamp's light. You fought the light instead of the cracks. Return when sealing from inside is braver than fighting from outside.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The cracked lamp's cracks are inside — so the sealing must be inside. The deity must enter the lamp to seal the cracks. The guardian starves when the cracks close — but sealing from inside means being inside when the cracks close.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Discordant Hierarchy. The Empyrean's chain of command has been corrupted. Each link in the chain now serves the Hollow. The hierarchy is inverting — the top serves the bottom of the Hollow.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hierarchy-constructs following corrupted commands. They obey because obedience is their nature — they cannot distinguish divine command from Hollow corruption.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The hierarchy-constructs obey corrupted commands. Do not destroy them — redirect them. They follow orders. Give them the right orders.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first link is restored. The original command is re-established. But the chain is damaged. The deeper chambers will test whether the command propagates.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The hierarchy-constructs obeyed corrupted commands. You destroyed them. Return when giving the right orders is more powerful than destroying the wrong followers.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Discordant Hierarchy tests whether the deity can distinguish divine command from corrupted command. The Hollow corrupted the method so the method became the purpose.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The corruption is spreading downward. Each corrupted link corrupts the one below. The hierarchy inverts — lower links command higher links. Chaos is the Hollow's preferred battlefield.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The constructs are inverting the hierarchy. Lower links command higher links. The inversion creates chaos.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The inverting hierarchy creates chaos. Do not fight chaos — restore a new order. One that does not depend on the chain.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The hierarchy-constructs are redirected — but the corruption lingers. The chain could re-invert.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The inverting hierarchy created chaos. You fought the chaos. Return when a new order is more powerful than fighting the old chaos.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The hierarchy-constructs obey because obedience is their nature. The defense is redirection, not destruction. Give them the right orders.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Dissonant Choir. Enter Broken Choir Chamber on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Broken Choir Chamber.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The inverted hierarchy has reached the trial road. Commands from above are now commands from the Hollow. The deity must disobey the hierarchy to follow the divine — but disobedience is the Hollow's domain.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow command-voices issuing corrupted commands in the voice of the hierarchy. Each command sounds legitimate — because the voice is real. The corruption is in the order, not the voice.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The command-voices sound legitimate. Do not obey the voice — obey the light. The voice is real. The order is not. The light is always real.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The command-voices are silenced — but their commands echo. The deeper chambers will be louder with corrupted orders.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The command-voices sounded legitimate. You obeyed the voice. Return when the light is the only voice you obey.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The command-voices are real voices issuing corrupted commands. The Hollow does not replace the voice. It replaces the order. The defense is to obey the light, not the voice.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The hierarchy's origin. The first link — the original command: 'serve the light.' The Hollow corrupted it to 'serve the chain.' The chain was the tool. Now the tool is the master.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The first link's guardian — a Hollow wearing the first commander's armor. It speaks the corrupted original command: 'serve the chain.'

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian speaks the corrupted command. Do not obey. The original was 'serve the light.' The chain was the method. The light was the purpose. When the method replaces the purpose, the hierarchy serves itself.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first link is reclaimed. The original command is restored — but the guardian's armor remains. The command is right. The armor is wrong.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The guardian's corrupted command held. You obeyed. Return when serving the light means breaking the chain.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The first command was 'serve the light.' The Hollow corrupted it to 'serve the chain.' When the method replaces the purpose, the hierarchy serves itself — and the Hollow feeds on self-service.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Radiance Trap. The Empyrean Gate's light is brighter than ever — but the brightness is the Hollow's. It has learned to imitate divine radiance perfectly. False light is indistinguishable from true.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: False-radiance constructs emitting divine-looking light that consumes. They look like allies. They feel like allies. They are not.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The false-radiance constructs look like allies. Do not see — feel. True light sustains. False light consumes. The difference is in the effect, not the appearance.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The false radiance is exposed — but not destroyed. It retreats into the deeper chambers. The next counterfeit will be closer.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The false-radiance constructs looked like allies. You trusted your eyes. Return when feeling is more powerful than seeing.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Radiance Trap tests whether the deity can distinguish true light from false when both look identical. The defense is feeling, not sight. True light sustains. False light consumes.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The false radiance is spreading. Each beam of false light looks like divine light, feels like divine light — but it consumes instead of sustains.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The constructs are blending true and false light. The partial truth makes the false part invisible. The blend is the trap.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The blended light is partially true. Do not trust the true part — it masks the false. Feel the consumption beneath the radiance.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The blended light is separated — but the blending technique is known to the Hollow. The deeper chambers will blend more seamlessly.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The blended light fooled you with partial truth. Return when consumption beneath radiance is always detectable.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The blended light — partially true, partially false — is the Hollow's most sophisticated Empyrean weapon. The partial truth makes the false part invisible. If it consumes, it is false — no matter how true it looks.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The false light has reached the trial road. Every step is lit — but which light is true? True light sustains. False light consumes. Both look identical. The deity must feel the difference.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow radiance-imitators copying the deity's own radiance perfectly. They look like the deity, radiate like the deity. But their light consumes.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The radiance-imitators copy you perfectly. Your light gives. Their light takes. The difference is direction, not radiance.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The radiance-imitators are dispersed — but they copied your radiance perfectly. The Hollow has your pattern.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The radiance-imitators copied you perfectly. Return when giving and taking are distinguishable in the radiance.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The radiance-imitators copy the deity perfectly. The defense is direction: the deity's light gives. The imitator's light takes. The feeling reveals the direction.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The radiance source. The Hollow has built a false first lamp — a perfect imitation of the celestial light's origin, radiating from the same position as the true lamp.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The false first lamp's guardian — a Hollow radiating perfect divine light, indistinguishable from the true keeper. The only difference: its light consumes.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian is indistinguishable from the true keeper. Do not look — feel. The true keeper's light sustains you. The false keeper's light drains you.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The false lamp is exposed — but not destroyed. The true lamp is dimmer. The deeper chambers will be lit by both — and distinguishing them will be harder.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The false lamp's guardian was indistinguishable. You looked instead of feeling. Return when the feeling of sustenance versus consumption is the only truth.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The false first lamp is indistinguishable by sight. The true lamp sustains. The false lamp consumes. The feeling requires vulnerability — the deity must let the light touch them to know whether it gives or takes.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise. Enter Heaven-Engine Apex on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Heaven-Engine Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Throne of Consumed Light. The final trial. Every fallen photon, every silenced voice, every corrupted command, every counterfeited radiance — all assembled into a throne of consumed light. The Hollow sits on it, radiating.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The Throne of Consumed Light. It radiates brighter than anything in the Gate. The brightness is real — and it consumes. Every photon that touches the deity drains them.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The throne radiates consumed light. Do not fight the light — out-give it. The throne's light takes. Your light gives. In a world of taking, giving is the revolution.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The Throne of Consumed Light is shattered. The stolen sources are freed — the first singer's voice, the first lamp's glow, the first commander's order, the first keeper's radiance. All restored. All giving. The Choir-Vault Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The throne's consumed light drained you. You fought the light. Return when giving is more powerful than fighting.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Throne of Consumed Light is the Hollow's ultimate Empyrean weapon: every stolen source of divine power, assembled into one throne. The brightest thing is the most dangerous — because brightness hides consumption.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise. Enter Heaven-Engine Apex on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Heaven-Engine Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Consumed Light Throne radiates divine-looking light that consumes everything it touches. It is the brightest object in the Empyrean Gate — and the brightest thing is the most dangerous.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The throne spawns consumed-light constructs — each made from a different stolen light source. The first singer's voice, the first lamp's glow, the first commander's radiance — all weaponized.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The consumed-light constructs are made of stolen sources. Do not destroy them — free them. Resonate with what they were before consumption.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The consumed-light constructs are freed. Each stolen source returns to its origin. All give. None consume.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The consumed-light constructs were stolen sources. You destroyed them. Return when resonance can free what consumption trapped.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The consumed-light constructs are stolen sources weaponized. The defense is resonance — the real source is still inside each construct. Resonate with what it was before consumption, and the source breaks free.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The throne has consumed the first singer's voice, the first lamp's light, the first commander's order, and the first keeper's radiance. It speaks with all their voices, radiates with all their light — all consumed, all Hollow.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow amalgam-singers singing with every consumed voice simultaneously. The harmony is perfect — because it is made of real voices. The perfect harmony consumes.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The amalgam-singers' harmony is perfect because it is real. Do not compete with perfection — compete with truth. Perfect harmony that consumes is not true harmony. True harmony gives.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The amalgam-singers fall silent — then sing again with their own voices. The imperfect harmony gives. The perfect harmony consumed. The Choir-Vault Gate recognizes the difference.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The amalgam-singers' perfect harmony overwhelmed you. Return when truth is more powerful than perfection.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The amalgam-singers' perfect harmony is made of real voices. But perfect harmony that consumes is not true harmony. True harmony gives. Imperfect harmony that gives defeats perfect harmony that takes.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The final confrontation. The throne's claim: it is the true source of the Empyrean's light. The original lamps were imperfect copies. Disprove it — with light that gives.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The throne itself — the brightest, loudest, highest. It claims to be the true source. Its light is real. Its light also consumes. Disprove it.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The throne claims to be the true source. Disprove it — not by being brighter, but by giving light where the throne takes it. The true source gives. The false source takes. The giving is the proof.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The throne's claim is disproved: it was not the true source. The true source gives. The throne took. The giving is the proof of truth. The Choir-Vault Gate stands — and the light that remains is the light that gives.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The throne's claim held. You could not disprove it. Return when the giving is the proof — when light that gives defeats light that takes.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Empyrean Gate's deepest truth: the true source gives. The false source takes. The throne was brighter — but brightness is not truth. The only truth is the giving. Light that gives is true light. No matter how bright, how loud, how high.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The choir has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign resonance-data. The silence knows which frequencies you used — and has learned to absorb them.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite silence-wraiths carrying your Normal campaign resonance-frequencies. They absorb the exact frequencies you used before.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The silence absorbs your old frequencies. Find new resonance. Speak a new truth.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: Chapter 1 holds — but the choir has recorded this resonance too. The deeper chambers will absorb it.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The silence absorbed your old frequencies. You resonated the same way. Return when new truth is more powerful than old resonance.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Elite Chapter 1 stores resonance-data across campaigns. Every Normal frequency becomes an Elite vulnerability.

missionIntro.text: The celestial light has been re-fallen with your Normal campaign reclamation patterns. The fallen shards now carry your reclamation technique — inverted.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The fallen shards carry your reclamation technique inverted. Each shard you try to reclaim now takes more light than it gives.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The fallen shards take more than they give. Give first, then reclaim. The Normal reclamation was pulling. The Elite must be pushing.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The fallen shards are reclaimed — but differently. The Gate has learned a new technique.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The fallen shards took more than they gave. You reclaimed by pulling. Return when giving before reclaiming is more powerful.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Gate's learning engine spans multiple campaigns. Each descent teaches the silence which frequencies the deity uses.

missionIntro.text: The hierarchy expects your Normal campaign commands. Every redirected construct has been re-corrupted with knowledge of how you redirected it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The re-corrupted constructs know your Normal campaign redirection method. They re-invert mid-execution.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The constructs re-invert mid-execution. Redirect with a command that is not an order but a resonance.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The constructs are redirected — but with resonance, not orders. The deeper chambers will have counter-resonance.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The constructs re-inverted mid-execution. You redirected with an order. Return when resonance is more powerful than command.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Elite constructs study Normal campaign redirection. The deity must create new resonance — because repetition is not resonance. It is echo.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The final trial of this chapter has been re-radiated. The Normal campaign victory is recorded — and the Elite version asks whether your light gave or whether the Gate reflected it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The re-radiated trial guardian speaks with your Normal campaign voice. It asks: did your light give, or did the Gate reflect it?

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian questions your light. Answer with light that gives without the Gate's help — light the Gate cannot reflect because it is already given.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The guardian falls — but the question remains. The Elite answer: the light gave because it was already given — because the Gate cannot reflect what has no receiver.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The guardian's question held. Return when given light is undeniable — when it cannot be reflected because it is already given.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: Each Elite victory teaches the Gate how to absorb the next deity's resonance. The choir is an archive of every frequency ever sung and every silence that learned to absorb it.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Dissonant Choir. Enter Broken Choir Chamber on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Broken Choir Chamber.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The final trial of this chapter has been re-radiated. The Normal campaign victory is recorded — and the Elite version asks whether your light gave or whether the Gate reflected it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The re-radiated trial guardian speaks with your Normal campaign voice. It asks: did your light give, or did the Gate reflect it?

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian questions your light. Answer with light that gives without the Gate's help — light the Gate cannot reflect because it is already given.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The guardian falls — but the question remains. The Elite answer: the light gave because it was already given — because the Gate cannot reflect what has no receiver.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The guardian's question held. Return when given light is undeniable — when it cannot be reflected because it is already given.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: Each Elite victory teaches the Gate how to absorb the next deity's resonance. The choir is an archive of every frequency ever sung and every silence that learned to absorb it.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Glass Stair War. Enter Glass Stair Ascent on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Glass Stair Ascent.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The choir has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign resonance-data. The silence knows which frequencies you used — and has learned to absorb them.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite silence-wraiths carrying your Normal campaign resonance-frequencies. They absorb the exact frequencies you used before.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The silence absorbs your old frequencies. Find new resonance. Speak a new truth.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: Chapter 4 holds — but the choir has recorded this resonance too. The deeper chambers will absorb it.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The silence absorbed your old frequencies. You resonated the same way. Return when new truth is more powerful than old resonance.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Elite Chapter 4 stores resonance-data across campaigns. Every Normal frequency becomes an Elite vulnerability.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise. Enter Heaven-Engine Apex on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Heaven-Engine Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Throne of Consumed Light has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign radiance. It now radiates YOUR light — brighter than you because it has no source to deplete. Your light, without your limit.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite Throne of Consumed Light with your Normal campaign radiance. It radiates your light without limit. Your light, without your limit.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The throne radiates your light without limit. Do not compete with limitlessness — give without source. Nothing cannot be consumed.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The throne is shattered for the last time. Your Normal campaign light is freed. The giving belonged to the act, not the source. The throne consumed the source. The act remains. The Choir-Vault Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The throne radiated your light without limit. You competed with limitlessness. Return when giving from nothing is more powerful than giving from a source.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Elite Throne of Consumed Light is the Empyrean Gate's ultimate trial: the deity's own giving, consumed and re-radiated. The disproof requires giving that has no source to consume.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield deity; roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.
visualDirection: Frame Heaven-Engine Apex as part of Choir-Vault Discord Ascent; faction-specific visual language and materials.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise. Enter Heaven-Engine Apex on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Heaven-Engine Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The throne uses your Normal campaign giving against you. Every photon you gave has been consumed and re-radiated. The throne gives your light — but the giving consumes the source, which is you.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The throne spawns constructs from your Normal campaign given light. Each one is a photon you gave — now weaponized.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The constructs are your given photons. Do not fight your own giving — give more. More giving overwhelms them.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The constructs are dissolved — your given photons return. The giving was yours — not because you were the source, but because you were the giver. The source can be consumed. The giver cannot.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The constructs were your given photons. You fought your own giving. Return when more giving overwhelms consumption.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The source-consumers reveal the Hollow's deepest Empyrean strategy: consume not the light but the source. The defense is giving from beyond the source — from the act. The act has no substance. It cannot be consumed.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield deity; roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.
visualDirection: Frame Heaven-Engine Apex as part of Choir-Vault Discord Ascent; faction-specific visual language and materials.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise. Enter Heaven-Engine Apex on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Heaven-Engine Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The throne speaks with four voices — the first singer, the first lamp, the first commander, AND your Normal campaign voice. All say: the giving belongs to the throne. The deity was the source.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow source-consumers consuming not the light but the source. The more you give, the more there is to consume.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The source-consumers eat the source, not the light. Do not protect the source — give from beyond it. The act has no source. The act cannot be consumed.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The source-consumers are starved. They consumed the source and found the giving continued. The act does not require a source. The act requires a choice.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The source-consumers ate the source. You protected the source. Return when giving from beyond the source — from the act — is visible.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Elite final claim resolves the Empyrean Gate's deepest question: does the giving belong to the giver or the source? The answer: the giving belongs to the act. The source was consumable. The act is not — because the act is a choice, and choice has no substance to consume.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Silent Seraph of Broken Praise. Enter Heaven-Engine Apex on Choir-Vault Discord Ascent through Choir-Vault Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Heaven-Engine Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The final Elite confrontation. The throne's claim: across both campaigns, the giving was the throne's — the deity was merely the source. Disprove it — with giving that has no source.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The final throne — radiating your light, speaking with your voice, giving with your truth. The claim: the giving belongs to the throne.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The throne claims the giving was its. Disprove it — with giving that has no source. The throne consumes sources. Choice has no substance. Choice cannot be consumed.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The Throne of Consumed Light is destroyed for the last time. The claim is disproved: the giving belonged to the act. The throne consumed the source. The act remains — sustained by choice, by giving, by light that comes from nothing except the choice to give.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The throne's claim held. Return when giving from choice — from nothing — from the act — is the only giving the throne cannot consume.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Elite Final Verdict: the giving does not belong to the source. It belongs to the act. The throne consumed the source and found the giving continued — because the giving was never the source's. It was the deity's choice — freely made, unconditionally given, inexhaustible because it comes from nothing except the choice to give.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Black-Iron Threshold. Enter Execution Sigil Court on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Execution Sigil Court.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The Black-Iron Gate reopens. The debt-ledger is exposed — every transaction, every bargain, every debt ever recorded. The Hollow has begun erasing entries. In the Infernal Gate, erased debts do not disappear. They become unowned.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Unowned obligations — floating debts with no creditor. They attach on contact. Once attached, they are binding.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The unowned obligations attach on contact. Do not touch them — fight around them. Or take ownership to control them — but ownership means accepting the debt.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The first ledger section is stabilized. The erased debts are re-owned — but the ledger is vast. The Hollow has learned which debts you take and which you assign.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The unowned obligations attached to you. You tried to avoid them. Return when taking ownership is more powerful than avoidance.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The Black-Iron Gate tests whether the deity can navigate a system of debts where creditors have been erased. Unowned debts are dangerous because they attach to anyone. The defense is ownership.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield deity; roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Black-Iron Threshold. Enter Execution Sigil Court on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Execution Sigil Court.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The erased debts are becoming unowned obligations — bindings with no creditor and no debtor. They float through the Gate, attaching to anyone who touches them.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The obligations are combining into compound debts. The compound debt is heavier and harder to avoid.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The compound debts are heavier. Do not avoid them — assign them. Restore the creditor — even if the creditor is you. A debt with an owner is controllable.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The unowned obligations are controlled — but more are being erased. The ledger is deteriorating faster than it can be restored.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The compound debts were too heavy. You tried to carry them. Return when assigning is more powerful than carrying.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The unowned obligations are the Hollow's most insidious Infernal weapon: debts with no creditor and no debtor. The defense is assignment — transfer the unowned to the Hollow.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield deity; roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Black-Iron Threshold. Enter Execution Sigil Court on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Execution Sigil Court.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The unowned obligations are multiplying. Each one that attaches to a traveler becomes their debt — unearned, unasked, but binding. The trial road is covered in floating debts.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow debt-collectors. They do not collect — they assign. They attach unowned obligations to the deity deliberately.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The debt-collectors assign obligations. Do not resist — re-assign. Transfer the unowned to the Hollow. The Hollow created them. Let the Hollow own them.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The debt-collectors are reassigned — but their assignment technique is recorded. The deeper chambers will have better assigners.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The debt-collectors assigned too many obligations. You resisted instead of re-assigning. Return when transfer is more powerful than resistance.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The debt-collectors assign obligations. The defense is re-assignment. The Infernal Gate is a system of transfers. The Hollow exploits by erasing creditors. The deity restores by becoming the creditor.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Black-Iron Threshold. Enter Execution Sigil Court on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Execution Sigil Court.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The ledger's core. The first transaction — the original debt that created the Infernal Gate. The Hollow has erased it. Without the original debt, the entire ledger system is destabilizing.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The erased original debt's guardian — a Hollow wearing the first debtor's chains. It speaks the erased transaction's terms — but the terms are corrupted. The original debt was voluntary. The corrupted terms are mandatory.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The guardian speaks corrupted terms. Do not argue — restore the original. The original debt was voluntary. The corruption makes it mandatory. Restore consent.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The original debt is partially restored — but the terms are still corrupted. The voluntary nature is remembered, but the corruption has made it feel mandatory.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The guardian's corrupted terms held. You argued with the corruption. Return when restoring consent is more powerful than arguing with coercion.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The original debt was voluntary. The Hollow corrupted it to mandatory. The difference is consent. Without consent, the transaction is not a debt. It is a theft.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Debt Ledger. Enter Debt Ledger Vault on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Debt Ledger Vault.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The Debt-Market. The Infernal Gate's trading floor has been breached. The Hollow is not stealing debts — it is giving them away. Free debts. Unowned. Unbinding.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Free-debt wraiths — unowned obligations given away by the Hollow. They are lighter than erased debts — but 'freely' by the Hollow means 'without consent from either party.'

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The free-debt wraiths are lighter. Do not accept them — even the useful ones. The Hollow's gifts are binding. The binding is in the acceptance, not the debt.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The market's first section is stabilized. The free debts are re-owned — but the flooding continues. The deeper chambers will have more free debts.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The original ledger's guardian — a Hollow erasing the ledger line by line, speaking the erased transactions as it erases them.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The Chain of Unpaid Debts. The Infernal Gate's enforcement mechanism has been corrupted. The Hollow has broken the chain's links, creating a cascade of unpaid debts that each generate their own chains.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Chain-constructs born from unpaid debts. Each one is a self-replicating binding that creates new debt with every contact. Touching one means owing one.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The chain-constructs create debt on contact. Do not touch them. In the Infernal Gate, contact is consent. Avoid contact to avoid consent.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The first chain is stabilized. The cascade is slowed — but the self-replicating chains remain. The deeper chambers will have faster cascades.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The chain-constructs created debt on contact. You touched them. Return when avoidance is more powerful than contact.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The Chain of Unpaid Debts tests whether the deity can navigate a system where enforcement has become self-replicating. A binding without consent replicates because it has no legitimate holder.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The guardian speaks the corrupted binding. Speak the original: 'I consent to be bound.' The consent is the binding. Without consent, the chain is slavery. Restore consent.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The Debtors' Revolt. The debtors of the Infernal Gate have been incited to revolt by the Hollow. The promise: break your chains and be free. The lie: breaking chains in the Infernal Gate creates new debt.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Revolting debtors breaking their chains. They are not enemies — they are victims of the Hollow's promise. Each believes they are being freed. Each is being more bound.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The revolting debtors are victims. Do not fight them — restore their chains. The chains were consensual. The breaking is not. Restore consent.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The first revolt is calmed. Some debtors restored their chains consensually. Some voided their debts. Both are legitimate. The deeper chambers will have more revolts.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The revolting debtors were victims. You fought them. Return when restoring is more powerful than fighting.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The Debtors' Revolt tests whether the deity can restore a system where enforcement has been weaponized through false liberation. Breaking chains creates more debt. The freedom is the trap.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The debtors break chains faster. Each broken chain creates a shockwave of new debt, destabilizing the Gate's ledger system.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The broken chains created shockwaves. You fought them instead of absorbing. Return when carrying and transferring is more powerful.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow revolutionaries inciting debtors to break chains. Each broken chain feeds the Hollow. The revolution is the feeding strategy.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The revolt's origin. The first debtor has been freed by the Hollow — but the freeing created a new debt: the debt of being freed without consent. The first debtor is more bound now than before.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The first debtor's liberator — a Hollow wearing the original creditor's face. It freed the debtor without consent. The debt of unwanted liberation is the largest debt in the Gate.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The liberator freed the debtor without consent. Do not re-bind — restore the consent. Ask. If the debtor consents to the original debt, the chain is restored. If not, the debt is void.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The first debtor is restored. The consent was asked — and the debtor chose the original debt. But the debt of unwanted liberation remains.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The liberator freed without consent. You re-bound without asking. Return when asking is more powerful than binding.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The debt of being freed without consent is the Infernal Gate's deepest lesson: freedom without consent is not freedom. It is a different kind of binding. Consent is the only resolution.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The Throne of Unowned Debt. The final trial. Every erased debt, every free obligation, every broken chain, every unconsented liberation — assembled into a throne of unowned debt. The Hollow sits on it, unbound.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The Throne of Unowned Debt radiating unowned obligations. The throne itself is the largest unowned obligation — binding the entire Gate to the Hollow.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The throne radiates unowned obligations. Do not resist them — own them. The Hollow un-owns to make them float. The defense is owning — consensually. An owned debt is not slavery.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The Throne of Unowned Debt is shattered. The unowned debts are re-owned — through new acts of consent. The first transaction, the original ledger, the first chain, the first debtor — all restored. All consensual. The Black-Iron Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The throne radiated unowned obligations. You resisted instead of owning. Return when consent is more powerful than resistance.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The Throne of Unowned Debt is the Hollow's ultimate Infernal weapon: every unowned obligation assembled into one throne. The disproof is not argument — it is act. A consensual transaction the throne cannot un-own.

missionIntro.text: The Unowned Debt Throne radiates unowned obligations. Every debt on it has no creditor and no debtor. The throne is the largest unowned obligation — binding the entire Gate to the Hollow.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The throne spawns unowned constructs — debts with no owner that attach to the deity, adding unconsensual weight.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The unowned constructs attach without consent. Do not remove them — consent to them. Consent transforms unowned obligation into consensual debt. The debt remains. The slavery does not.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The unowned constructs are dissolved — through consent. The deity owned each one consensually. The ownership transformed slavery into transaction. The debt remains. The slavery does not.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The unowned constructs attached without consent. You removed them. Return when consent transforms slavery into transaction.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The unowned constructs attach without consent. The defense is consent. Consent transforms unowned obligation into consensual debt. The debt is not the slavery. The absence of consent is the slavery.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The throne has consumed the first transaction, the original ledger, the first chain, and the first debtor's consent. All say: all debt is unowned. All binding is without consent. The Infernal Gate is a system of slavery.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow un-owners erasing ownership from every debt the deity holds. Each erased ownership turns consensual debt into unowned obligation.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The un-owners erase ownership. Do not protect old ownership — create new. Each re-owning is a new act of consent. The Hollow un-owns. The deity re-owns.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The un-owners are starved. They erased ownership — and the deity re-owned. Consent cannot be erased because it is not a thing. It is a choice. The choice was made.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The un-owners erased your ownership. You protected it. Return when re-owning is more powerful than protecting.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The un-owners erase ownership. The defense is re-owning — creating new ownership through new acts of consent. Consent cannot be erased because it is not a thing. It is an act.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The final confrontation. The throne's claim: all debt is slavery. All consent is coerced. Disprove it — with a consensual transaction the throne cannot un-own.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The throne speaking with four voices: the first transaction, the first ledger, the first chain, the first debtor. All say: all debt is slavery.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The throne claims all debt is slavery. Disprove it — with a consensual transaction. The throne cannot un-own a transaction where both parties consent. Consent is a choice. Choices cannot be erased.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The throne's claim is disproved: not all debt is slavery. Debt without consent is slavery. Debt with consent is a transaction. The difference is consent. The Black-Iron Gate stands — sustained by consent, by choice, by agreement.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The throne's claim held. You could not disprove it. Return when a consensual transaction is undeniable — when consent proves debt is not slavery.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The Throne of Unowned Debt has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign consent. It carries your consent as its foundation — your Normal campaign consensual transactions, consumed and un-owned. The throne claims YOUR consent proves all consent is coerced.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite Throne of Unowned Debt with your Normal campaign consent. Your consensual transactions, weaponized as evidence of coercion.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The throne uses your consent against you. Do not deny your old consent — re-consent. New consent is the answer. Create consent it has not seen.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The throne is shattered for the last time. Your Normal campaign consent is freed. The consent was not coerced. The proof: you consented again, differently, creating something new. Coercion repeats. Consent creates. The Black-Iron Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The throne uses your Normal campaign consent to un-own ALL consent. Each consensual transaction is presented as evidence that consent under the Gate is always coerced. Your choices, weaponized against choice itself.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The throne spawns constructs from your Normal campaign consent. Each is a consensual transaction you performed — now un-owned and presented as coerced.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The constructs are your transactions re-labeled as coerced. Do not defend old consent — perform new consent. The defense of consent is not argument. It is act.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The constructs are dissolved. Your transactions are restored — not as evidence of coercion, but as proof of choice. Coerced consent repeats identically. Free consent creates anew.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The constructs were your transactions re-labeled. You defended your old consent. Return when new consent is more powerful than defending.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The consent-corrupters re-label consent as compliance. Compliance repeats. Consent creates. The defense is not arguing that consent was free — it is demonstrating freedom through creation.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Volcanic Glass Magistrate. Enter Volcanic Glass Courtroom on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Volcanic Glass Courtroom.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The throne speaks with five voices — the first transaction, the first ledger, the first chain, the first debtor, AND your Normal campaign voice. All say: all consent is coerced.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow consent-corrupters re-labeling consent as compliance. Each act of consent becomes compliance. The re-labeling is the weapon.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The consent-corrupters re-label consent as compliance. Do not resist — demonstrate the difference. Compliance repeats. Consent creates. Create something new.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The consent-corrupters are starved. They re-labeled consent as compliance — but the deity created. Compliance cannot create. Only consent can. The creation is the proof.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The consent-corrupters re-labeled everything. You resisted. Return when creating is more powerful than resisting.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The Elite final claim resolves the Infernal Gate's deepest question: is consent under the Gate's pressure truly free? The answer: consent that creates is free. Consent that repeats is compliance. The difference is creation.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Volcanic Glass Magistrate. Enter Volcanic Glass Courtroom on Black-Iron Debt Descent through Black-Iron Gate. Objective: With one selected deity, advance through Volcanic Glass Courtroom.

missionIntro.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
missionIntro.text: The final Elite confrontation. The throne's claim: across both campaigns, your consent proves the Gate coerces. Disprove it — with consent that no Gate could coerce.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
enemyIntroduction.text: The final throne — speaking with five voices. The claim: your consent proves all consent is coerced. Disprove it.

midBattle.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
midBattle.text: The throne claims all consent is coerced. Disprove it — with consent that creates. Coercion cannot create. Only consent can. The creation is the proof.

victory.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
victory.text: The Throne of Unowned Debt is destroyed for the last time. The claim is disproved: consent that creates is free. Consent that repeats is compliance. The Infernal Gate stands — sustained by consent that creates, by choice that produces, by freedom that generates. The consent was free because the creation was new.

defeat.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
defeat.text: The throne's claim held. Return when consent that creates — consent that produces something new — is the undeniable proof of freedom.

codex.speaker: Celiane Debt-Scrivener
codex.text: The Elite Final Verdict: consent is not coerced because it occurs under pressure. Consent is coerced when it repeats what the pressure demands. Consent is free when it creates what the pressure could not demand. Coercion repeats. Consent creates. The creation is the proof. The consent was free because the creation was new.
